title: Plan: bring the Pipeline's own source under the module, layering and size rules it imposes, without new drift or status problems
goal: PO REQUEST 2026-11-19 and PO EXCEPTION FROM THE MODEL DEFAULT (model claude-fable-5-2): the Pipeline requires modular, agent-suited architecture of the projects it governs (modules with declared dependencies, at most 1000 lines per hand-written source file, no import of a module that is not declared) but its own source does not meet those rules, and it is to be released with a clean architecture. Produce the DETAILED PLAN to get there. THE PO'S CENTRAL RISK, which the plan must be built around: the rebuild itself must never create new drift or new status problems, because a user repository that ends in an inconsistent map, ADR, baseline or lifecycle state blocks itself and other repositories. DELIVERABLE: ONE new markdown document, specs/sprint-alfred-epic/plans/architecture-fitness-remediation-plan-2026-11-19.md, in English, no code change anywhere, no new test other than the check file named in the package. It is a PLAN, not an implementation. READ-ONLY SOURCES: the real checkout (it holds candidate 32), starting with backlog/items/2026-11-19-the-pipeline-does-not-meet-the-module-and-size-rules-it-imposes-on-projects.md (the measured picture: 64 of 1160 hand-written source files over the 1000-line bound holding 37 percent of the code, 14 over 2000 and four over 5000 lines, 103 size exceptions in architecture/boundary-policy.json some already outgrown, the whole plugin as ONE module pipeline-core of about 1030 files, 38 files of plugins/pipeline-core/lib importing from plugins/pipeline-core/scripts, nine folder pairs importing each other, god files with high fan-in: lib/worktree-lifecycle.mjs 71 importers, lib/onboarding-continuity.mjs 42, scripts/pipeline-state.mjs 29, and the check reporting 125 findings after the exemptions of candidate 32: 50 oversize non-test files, 74 unowned paths in the top-level scripts folder, 1 forbidden dependency). RE-MEASURE every number yourself with plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/architecture-boundary-check.mjs --root . --json and plain rg/git reads before you rely on it, and correct the item where it is wrong. ALSO READ: architecture/map/*.md, architecture/boundary-policy.json, architecture/fitness-model.json, architecture/baseline.json, architecture/adoption-state.json, project/architecture-decisions.compiled.json, docs/adr/ (the ADR sidecars that name a module id, for example docs/adr/0009-session-hygiene-lifecycle.json), docs/operating-model.md, docs/state.md, docs/adr/README.md, the plugin scripts and guards that read or require the map (scripts/module-inventory.mjs, scripts/generate-architecture-overview.mjs, scripts/architecture-baseline.mjs, scripts/architecture-fitness.mjs, scripts/architecture-boundary-check.mjs, scripts/architecture-adoption.mjs, hooks/guard-push.mjs, lib/architecture-entry-readiness.mjs, lib/architecture-design.mjs, lib/architecture-effective-decisions.mjs, hooks/guard-lifecycle-ready.mjs, scripts/check-vendored-template-sync.mjs), docs/operating-tools.md (section on the clone-slice route), plugins/pipeline-core/skills/pipeline-start/references/happy-path.md and workflow-dispatch.md, and the held-patch notes under specs/sprint-alfred-epic/evidence/held-patches/. THE QUESTIONS THE PLAN MUST ANSWER: (1) which target structure (modules, their responsibilities and allowed dependencies, a layer order such as lib below scripts and hooks) is the smallest one that makes the map true, and how is it derived from what the code really does; (2) in what ORDER can the work be done so that EVERY intermediate commit leaves the map, the ADR module scoping, the baseline, the fitness model, the boundary policy exceptions, the generated overview, the adoption state, the capability inventory and the Reader inputs mutually consistent and every guard green; name for each stage which of these derived or mirrored copies changes and how it is refreshed in the same commit; (3) what happens to artifacts that name the module id pipeline-core today (fitness-model.json, boundary-policy.json, ADR sidecars with module applicability, project/architecture-decisions.compiled.json, map concept files, baseline.json, any receipt or digest that binds the map): a migration or read-compatibility plan per artifact, so that no existing signed or digest-bound record becomes unreadable, orphaned or stale; (4) what a USER repository sees: user repositories carry their own maps and policies and may run an older plugin version beside a newer one; state exactly what changes for them at each stage, what an older and a newer plugin each read of the other's files, and prove that no stage can put a user repository in a blocked state (no new refusal without a runnable repair, no required PO action that did not exist before; the PO rule: every refusal needs a repair the agent or the PO can actually run); (5) how to restore the layering (no file in lib importing from scripts, no folder cycle) and keep it restored by a rule the boundary check enforces, including how the existing 38 importers are handled one by one or by group; (6) how to split the oversize files in dependency order (fan-in times size) as behaviour-preserving slices: for each of the top 12 files the proposed seams (responsibilities, not line cuts), the public entry that must stay importable under its old path (re-export shim or not, and when the shim is removed), the existing suites that pin its behaviour (name them by path; count them), and the protected or guard-owned files among them with the route they need (protected-source route, PO signature steps), plus which slices can run in PARALLEL because their write scopes do not overlap and which must be serial; (7) how the size exceptions in boundary-policy.json are retired without raising any ratchet, and which test files and generated artifacts are exempt (candidate 32 exempts test files from the hard bound and generated files such as bundles, minified files and dist output from every check); (8) how the release proves it: the measured numbers (files over the bound, lines held by them, exception count, lib-to-scripts imports, mutually importing folder pairs, unowned paths) to record as release evidence, a rule that makes the Pipeline's own check fail when one of them grows, and what the release notes may honestly say if only part is done. WHAT THE DOCUMENT MUST CONTAIN: (A) the verified measurements with the exact command that produced each number; (B) the target architecture (modules, allowed dependencies, layers) with the evidence from the code for each boundary and the list of things you could not decide from code alone; (C) the DRIFT-SAFETY ANALYSIS: a table of every artifact bound to the module structure (name, file, what binds it, how drift would show, which guard or check reads it, the migration or read-compat step) and, for each stage of the plan, the invariant that holds after it and the command that proves it; (D) the staged plan in dependency order: slices of at most one Goldfish dispatch each, each with its write scope (repo-relative paths), what it leaves unchanged, the suites that prove it, a rollback story, whether it touches protected paths, whether it can run in parallel with which other slices, and its size (S/M/L); mark the first three slices that are safe to start now and the stages that must wait for a PO decision; (E) the USER-REPOSITORY compatibility statement per stage; (F) the decisions only the PO can take (each with your recommendation) and the list of things you could NOT verify (say so plainly; never fill a gap with a guess). QUALITY BAR: every claim names its file and, where possible, the function or constant; numbers are counted, not estimated; prefer deleting a rule, copy or state to adding one; a stage that adds a new schema, status, writer or mirrored copy must say what it removes; a stage that cannot be made drift-safe must be cut smaller or reordered until it can, and the plan must say so. HARD LIMITS: no change to any file other than the one deliverable and the check file; no private consumer project or feature name and no machine path anywhere (neutral ids only, repo-relative paths); do not propose to weaken, skip or auto-approve any gate, signature, push approval or Critic evidence; do not propose a change that alters the digest of an existing record without a read-compat plan; do not propose raising a size ratchet. The six section headings are exactly: '## A. Measurements', '## B. Target architecture', '## C. Drift-safety analysis', '## D. Staged plan', '## E. User-repository compatibility', '## F. Decisions and unverified items'.
